reviews.title: A good core experience
reviews.text:
It’s a shame that this is pitched as “an AI browser”, because the AI integration is actually the least interesting and least useful thing about it. What keeps me tethered to Arc Search — in spite of The Browser Company ruthlessly abandoning their beloved niche desktop browser Arc in favor of chasing LLM money — is the simple genius of its design. It opens right up to a search bar, tabs are easy to manage and close, incognito can be switched on or off with the press of a single button. Everything about Arc Search is incredibly responsive and easy to do.

I hope that one day the AI bubble bursts and these talented developers will be free to focus all their energy on designing great apps again.

reviews.title: The tabs view is dated and unhelpful
reviews.text:
It shows tabs as giant cards, which is so dated and a pain to scroll through. Please give the options for grid and list views. This looks even more ridiculous on the iPad. It makes the whole app just seem like a blown up phone app, which should be an embarrassment for the devs.  And there’s no tab grouping, way to search through tabs, or obvious way to send pages to a space. This is basically just a handy way to view what’s open on your desktop if you’re syncing, but it’s not a serious browser to use as your main on the phone or iPad.

There’s also no user agent control and no way to clear browser data on a per-site basis.  It's all or nothing. This really annoys me on sites that auto-log me in to my Google account. If I want to switch accounts on that site I have to wipe all cookies for the whole browser, or just switch to a different browser which is what I would do.

reviews.title: A sad goodbye to what was the best browser
reviews.text:
I’ve waited as long as possible before leaving this review because I loved Arc that much. It completely changed how I browsed the web, and I used to look forward to every release note.

Unfortunately, ever since the team pivoted and left desktop Arc behind, I’ve been forced to move on. I spent months trying to make Dia work, but it doesn't replace what made Arc special. There was easily room for both browsers to exist side-by-side. It’s been such a letdown hoping for a comeback that never arrived. Please reconsider and bring Arc development back.

reviews.title: Best Browser
reviews.text: Arc is seriously amazing. Such simple differences from safari or chrome but they actually make a world of a difference. Just simple little changes that you wouldn’t think of when using other browsers but as soon as you are on Arc, you’re just like wow, why don’t other browsers do this? I love the organization in spaces, the customization on desktop, simple and actually nice to use AI, amazing UX design, shortcuts that make sense, syncing mobile and desktop is great, the ad and pop up blocking without downloading extensions is flawless. I just love Arc and won’t ever be switching after trying it out.

reviews.title: Loved it a lot before but now it’s getting worse
reviews.text: Coming from Google Search which drained my battery too quickly, I switched to Google with Arc Search and overall I have gotten better results with my phone battery. However over time, I have noticed that this app has gotten worse. Sometimes the curser in the search bar disappears when I am searching something. This makes it frustrating to move the typing indicator when editing text in the search bar and when you can’t even see it. This app has gotten much slower over time too. I feel like it has gotten harder and harder to find a fast browser. JavaScript purging is slow as molasses on Arc, even reloading Wiki can sometimes take 10-15 seconds even with perfect low Wi-Fi latency and fast speed. Wiki is a lightweight website and on a modern iPhone 17 Pro with a A19 Pro processor, it should only take less than half a second. I never understood why server lag has gotten worse on so many browsers lately too which contributes to this slow speed. The app also crashes sometimes when I multitask or search something too quickly. Overall, while I loved Arc at the beginning, I feel like it has lost its charm overtime with these bugs and slow performance and I hope it gets fixed.

reviews.title: Goodbye
reviews.text:
Thanks for trying to bring the best browser to the world, and deeply failing in it.

What else can I say about your success in selling the company, dropping your main product to make an AI bloatware that nobody asked for? Arc started with so much promise—a fresh take on browsing, actual innovation, things we didn't know we needed. Then you decided "let's fix what isn't broken" and gave us... another Chromium wrapper with chatbot integration.

The vertical tabs were nice while they lasted. The spaces concept? Actually clever. But somewhere along the way you forgot that a browser's job is to browse the web, not to be a playground for your AI experiments. Now it's sluggish, overengineered, and trying to be everything at once—which means it does nothing well.

Congrats on the exit, I guess. Shame about the product.
